div.l: At onys in thys herborow as now
Feyne wolde I do you myrthe yf I wyste how
And of a myrthe I am right now be thought
To do you ese and it shal coste you nought
Ye go to Caunterbury ward god you spede
The blysful martyr quyte you your mede
And wel ye woot as ye go be the weye
Ye shappyn you to talke and to pleye
For trewly comfort ne myrthe is non
To ryde by the wey dombe as a stoon
And therfore wyl I make you dysport
As I sayde erst and do you comfort
And yf it liketh you alle by one assent
Forto stonde at my Iugement
And forto werke as I shal you say
To morow whan ye ryden on the way
Now by my fader soule that is ded
But ye be mery I shal yeue you my hed
Hold vp your hond wythoute more speche
Our counsel shal not longe be to seche
Vs thought it was not worth to make vs wys
And graunted hym wythoute more a vys
And bad hym saye hys verdyt as hym lyst
Lordynges quod he now herkeneth for the best
But take it not I pray you in dysdeyne
Thys is the poynt to speke it short and pleyne
That eche of you to shorte wyth your weye
In thys vyage shal telle talis tweye
To Cauntirburyward I mene it soo
And homward he shal telle other talis two
Of auenturis that whilom haue befalle
And whyche of you beryth hym best of alle
That is to saye that tellyth in thys caas
Tales of best sentence and most solaas
Shal haue a souper of oure alther cost
Here in thys place sittynge by thys post
Whan that we come ayen from Caunterbury
And forto make you the more mery
